nodes.label: Share the roadway with people walking or cycling, motorcycles, large trucks, animal riders and slow vehicles as well as passenger cars.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: Use exceptional care around pedestrians, particularly near schools, bus stops, playgrounds and parks, and remain prepared to yield.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: A pedestrian in a crosswalk or crossing a driveway or alley entrance along a sidewalk has the stated right of way.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: Pedestrians should use intersection crosswalks, obey pedestrian controls and look in both directions before crossing.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: Without a sidewalk, pedestrians should walk along the left side facing approaching traffic.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.no_confusable_reason: No single interchangeable alternative is asserted for this complete source condition; related requirements keep separate nodes and their exact qualifiers.

nodes.label: At night, a person walking should use white or light clothing or carry a light; walking on interstate or limited-access highways is prohibited.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Expect people to emerge between parked or stopped vehicles and inspect the path for pedestrians before backing.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Comply with school-zone speed requirements when children or flashing school lights are present, and stop and yield when directed by a crossing guard.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Stop fully when a person with a white cane or harnessed guide dog is attempting to cross the road, and proceed afterward with particular care.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A visually impaired pedestrian may listen for a vehicle to stop before crossing; do not honk or shout at that pedestrian.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Bicycles using the road are vehicles whose riders share the traffic-law responsibilities, privileges and rights of motor-vehicle drivers.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The passing-clearance rule treats at least three feet as reasonable and prudent when motor traffic is moving at thirty miles per hour or less.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Above thirty miles per hour, the bicycle-clearance requirement adds another foot for each additional ten miles per hour.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Yield to bicyclists in intersections and where a bicycle path or lane crosses a road.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not drive, stop or park in a designated bicycle lane or path except for driveway or alley access, official duties, police direction or an emergency.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Reduce speed and maximize practical room when passing a bicyclist, allowing the cyclist to clear an intersection before turning.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Avoid sudden slowing or stops directly in front of a bicycle because a motor vehicle's stronger brakes can contribute to a collision.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not sound a horn close to a bicyclist unless a collision threatens, since the sound may startle the rider into your path.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Watch for bicyclists entering the lane, particularly children moving from sidewalks into the road.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Never make a sharp turn across a bicyclist's path or force the rider off the roadway.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Although riders are required to follow traffic direction, search for bicycles throughout the roadway rather than assuming each rider is correctly positioned.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Rain, sand and gravel affect bicycles particularly strongly, so use extra caution when sharing those surfaces.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A bicyclist normally signals turns and stops by hand but may need both hands for control; watch head movements or shoulder checks for additional clues.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before opening a parked vehicle's door or backing, check side and rear areas for bicycles, especially near homes or schools.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Motorcyclists have the same roadway rights and responsibilities as other drivers but their narrow profile can hide them in blind spots and complicate speed judgments.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Give a motorcycle the entire lane and do not attempt to travel beside it within that lane.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Before turning left across opposing traffic, carefully identify any motorcycle and judge its approach speed.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Leave at least four seconds of following time behind a motorcycle.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Confirm that a motorcyclist is actually turning rather than relying on an operating turn signal, since it may not cancel automatically.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Bad weather and slippery surfaces may cause a motorcyclist to change speed or course, and wet-road glare can be particularly difficult at night.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Crosswinds and air blasts from fast large trucks can shift a motorcycle's path, especially on bridges or exposed highway stretches.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Uneven pavement, gravel, debris, seams, grooves or covers can affect a motorcycle's travel; metal or grated bridge surfaces may cause wobbling.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A rear orange-and-red reflective or fluorescent triangle marks an animal-drawn, farm or construction vehicle traveling below twenty-five miles per hour.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Approach a slow vehicle carefully and pass only after ensuring the maneuver is safe.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Watch rural roads for farm machinery crossing or moving along the highway and do not expect its operator to hear your approach.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Animal-drawn vehicles and horse riders share road-use rights and traffic-rule duties with motor vehicles.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Near a horse, slow down, assess the situation and pass carefully without sounding the horn or revving the engine.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Large commercial vehicles maneuver less easily than cars and generally have larger blind spots and longer acceleration and stopping distances.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A large truck or bus needs additional turning room, so leave enough space for its maneuver.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The no-zone means the front, rear and side blind areas where a truck or bus driver cannot see nearby vehicles.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A truck's right-side blind area can begin behind the cab and extend along the vehicle's full length; avoid staying beside it longer than necessary.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: If the truck driver's face is not visible in the side mirror, assume the driver cannot see your vehicle.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook's ideal-condition example gives a loaded truck at fifty-five miles per hour at least three hundred thirty-five feet to stop, even with good tires and adjusted brakes.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Avoid entering the road or changing lanes close in front of a large vehicle because it needs more distance to stop.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: After passing a large vehicle, wait until its full front appears in your rearview mirror before returning ahead of it and maintaining speed.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Rear blind spots behind a large vehicle may extend as far as two hundred feet, so avoid close following and position where its side mirrors can reveal your vehicle.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Where practical, avoid the right lane near weigh-station exits or steep hills to give slow large vehicles room to join or use that lane.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A truck or bus may swing left before a right turn and use space in adjoining lanes; never squeeze between it and the curb.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Wait until the large vehicle completes its turn instead of trying to turn through its maneuvering space.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When meeting an oncoming truck, keep safely to the right to reduce side-contact risk and the effect of air turbulence between vehicles.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: If uncertain about an approaching truck's or bus's speed, do not turn left across its path because it needs more stopping room than a car.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Stop behind the marked intersection line so that a turning large vehicle has the room the marking preserves.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Never cut off a large vehicle to reach a turn or exit or to get ahead of it at a one-lane construction area.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Yield to an emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights from any direction by moving right and stopping without obstructing an intersection.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: After the emergency vehicle passes, signal before reentering the roadway and do so only when safe.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Keep at least five hundred feet behind a fire truck using warning lights or a siren, and do not drive or park in the block where it has stopped for a fire alarm.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: At a highway emergency, traffic stop or stopped vehicle displaying warnings, reduce speed and provide a wide berth when practical without endangering opposing traffic.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When traffic allows it safely, move into a lane away from the incident or emergency personnel and promptly leave a lane that is wholly or partly blocked.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Follow authorized traffic directions and emergency signals around a crash, fire, maintenance activity or other roadway emergency.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A move-over-law violation brings a fine and penalty assessment, with a larger fine for another offense within twelve months.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: For a police traffic stop, pull aside, stop fully and select park; stay inside unless the officer requests that you leave.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Switch off the engine, activate hazard lamps and, at night, illuminate the interior during the described police stop.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Remain calm and belted, ask passengers to do likewise, keep hands on the wheel and limit unnecessary movement.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: When an officer requests license and registration documents, explain where they are before reaching slowly while keeping one hand on the wheel.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: For an unmarked police vehicle, check that its blue lights are activated; an officer without a uniform can be asked for a badge or department identification.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Work zones can involve closed lanes, detours, workers and moving machinery, creating hazards from narrow lanes and rough pavement.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Watch orange work-zone signs, cones, barrels, large vehicles and workers, and reduce speed even without a newly posted lower limit.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Increase following space in a work zone, monitor surrounding traffic and remain ready to stop.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Use exceptional caution at night in a work zone even when no workers are visible.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Adjust lane position to leave room for workers and construction equipment and follow the posted work-zone instructions.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Do not return to normal speed until the End Road Work sign is visible.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Plan for work-zone delays, depart early and use an alternate route when one is available.
